fields.name: datum_type
fields.documentation: How this value is encoded -- the ONE place the value type lives (a body never repeats it). REQUIRED in practice whenever the value has a byte representation (`data_body` true, or an inline numeric payload); absent for a term or an inline composite with no numeric payload.

fields.name: source_datum_type
fields.documentation: The source's own spelling, OMITTED when it is already canonical. Kept because the map is NOT invertible -- `bool` maps back to `logical` OR `ubit1`, and `char` has no canonical at all -- so retaining it makes the normalisation AUDITABLE: the corpus can be queried afterwards to verify every `float64` came from a `double` rather than from a default.

fields.name: data_body
fields.documentation: True: this value's bytes are in data_body documents that point here through `owner_id`. False (the default): the value is inline in `value`, or absent. A document marked true with no body pointing at it has lost its data -- the batch check (item 60).

rules.name: datum_type_when_bytes
rules.statement: `datum_type` is present whenever the value has bytes: an inline numeric or text array, or `data_body` true.
